meta.name: xcode-zenix
meta.label: Xcode Dark · macOS Sonoma
meta.comment: The original zenix palette: Xcode Dark for the editor and TUI family, Apple's macOS Sonoma dark-mode system colours for the compositor, bar, greeter and popups. Every value here was extracted from the hand-written configs, so selecting this theme reproduces them byte for byte.

terminal.comment: Slots mapped the Xcode way: teal in 2, mint in 10. Drives ghostty, and through it eza, fd, bat, fastfetch and every TUI without a theme of its own.

washes.comment: White laid over whatever is behind, by weight. These are lifts, not colours -- the cards are blurred by hl.layer_rule and opaque surfaces would destroy that. On a light theme they arrive as dark-alpha instead.

css.comment: Spelled exactly as the stylesheets spell them -- decimal rgba() for GTK. These become @define-color declarations in waybar-style.css and wofi/style.css.

hypr.comment: Packed-hex rgba() and an ARGB literal for the shadow -- hyprland's own spellings. The borders are white-alpha rather than a palette colour: a neutral highlight over any wallpaper.

hyprlock.comment: Mixed spellings on purpose: hyprlock takes decimal rgba() for the background fallback and packed hex everywhere else. `placeholder` is Pango markup inside the config, so its `#` is doubled to survive hyprlang's comment parsing.

sddm.comment: Keys read by Main.qml and ThemedCombo.qml through SDDM's `config` object. The washes are the white-alpha fills the QML used to carry inline.

waybar.comment: Pango markup colours: the clock's calendar in waybar-config.jsonc and the agenda script's own spans.

btop_ramps.comment: btop draws each meter as a three-stop gradient. These are hand-tuned darkenings of the end colour rather than anything derivable, so they are stored rather than computed. free/download share a ramp, as do cached/upload.

apps.comment: Theme *names*, not colours. `qt_scheme` is an absolute path when it names one of qt6ct's own schemes, or a bare theme name when the palette ships in qt6ct/colors/.
